raw_response:
I am 65 years old, I never went to school. I learned everything from my father and from doing it with my own hands for 40 years. I have 13.1 mu in Quzhou County, and I grow wheat after National Day and maize after wheat harvest. My son works in a factory in Handan, so it is just me and my wife at home. We hire two people from the village for wheat harvest and for a few days at maize planting when it is busy. I watch what my neighbors do — that is how I know what works.

For my wheat: I sow about 30 jin of improved seed per mu, the same kind that Old Wang across the road uses. His wheat always looks thick and strong. At planting, I spread half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that is 25 kg per mu. The bag has some numbers on it, but I do not read well, so I just ask the dealer for the same kind as last year. Then in March, when the wheat turns green, I broadcast 20 kg of urea per mu. At the jointing stage in April, I put another 15 kg of urea per mu. Last year I used this exact amount and got 1000 jin per mu. Some young people tell me I use too much, but I saw what happened to Li Laohan two years ago when he tried to save money on fertilizer — his wheat was thin and yellow, and he lost half his crop. A bag of fertilizer costs 100 yuan. Losing a harvest costs thousands. I would rather waste some fertilizer than risk going hungry.

I water the wheat three times: once before the winter freeze, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. My well has enough water, so I do not worry about that. For spraying, I go out three times total — once for weeds, once for bugs, and once for that rust disease if I see the leaves turning orange.

For the maize: Right after wheat harvest in early June, I plant hybrid maize seed. Everyone uses hybrid now — you cannot get good yield with the old seed. I plant about one small package per mu. I do not till the field; I plant straight into the wheat stubble. It saves diesel and time, and my neighbor has done no-tillage for five years with good results. At planting, I put 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow. When the maize is knee-high, at the big trumpet stage, I side-dress 20 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once when the plants are small if it is dry, and once at flowering. Last year I watered twice. I spray three times: herbicide once, and insecticide twice for the corn borer. Those worms will eat the heart out of the plant if you let them.

I use the rotary tiller before wheat planting because the maize stalks and roots are thick and the soil needs breaking up. For maize, no-tillage is fine — the wheat stubble is soft.

I think about my whole budget. Fertilizer is my biggest expense, then hired labor at harvest. I do not buy the most expensive pesticide; I buy the one that worked last year. If I spend too much on one thing, I have less for another, so I stick to what I know. This year I will do exactly what I did last year. Change is risky.

I expect 1000 jin per mu — that is 500 kg — for wheat, and 1100 jin per mu — that is 550 kg — for maize. That is what I got last year, and that is what I will get this year if the weather cooperates.
